P3_note: S2 (N=3) is explicitly flagged small_sample_flag=true. Per mission instruction, this diagnosis does NOT conclude S2 should be removed based on three observations -- it is reported descriptively only.
P4_finding: The ASIAN_LONDON (-0.672R) vs LONDON_NEWYORK (+0.262R) expectancy gap is associated with a large SL-rate difference (53.3% vs 18.75%) and a modestly different setup composition (ASIAN_LONDON: S1=6/S2=1/S3=8, more S3-weighted; LONDON_NEWYORK: S1=7/S2=2/S3=7, more balanced). Friction is NOT a differentiator (0.208R vs 0.173R mean, both close to the overall 0.190R average). MAE is deeper in ASIAN_LONDON (-0.738R vs -0.543R mean) and MFE is markedly lower (0.463R vs 0.999R mean) -- consistent with ASIAN_LONDON occurrences both stopping out more often AND running less favorably when they don't. Because setup composition differs between the two sessions, this diagnosis cannot cleanly isolate a pure 'session effect' from a 'setup-mix effect' with only 15 and 16 occurrences respectively.
P5_finding: 11 SL occurrences (net expectancy -1.224R) are concentrated in ASIAN_LONDON (8/11) and further cluster on specific calendar days: 3 of 11 SL occurrences fall on 2026-05-26 alone (07:30, 08:45, 09:00) and 2 more on 2026-06-01 (07:30, 09:00) -- 45% of all SL occurrences land on just 2 of the 33 development days. Mean MAE for SL trades is -0.593R (median -0.894R, bimodal: several trades show MAE=MFE=0.0, i.e. an immediate/near-instant stop-out with zero prior excursion in either direction -- both S2 SL trades and at least one other show this exact pattern -- versus others that ran favorably first). 4 of 11 SL occurrences (36%) reached MFE >= 0.5R before eventually stopping out, and 1 of 11 reached MFE >= 1.0R -- i.e. a minority of SL trades had meaningful favorable excursion that reversed; the majority did not.
P6_finding: Mean MFE across all 31 occurrences is 0.739R against a mean realized gross_R of essentially 0.0003R -- a mean gap of 0.739R (median 0.619R) between favorable excursion reached and what was actually realized. 12 of 31 occurrences (39%) show positive MFE but a realized gross_R at or below zero -- i.e. the trade moved favorably at some point but still closed flat or negative. The 'capture ratio' (mean of gross_R/MFE_R, -1.12) is not a meaningful summary on its own -- it is dominated by sign flips from trades where gross_R went negative after a small positive MFE, and is reported here only for completeness, not as a primary finding. The gap-based framing (MFE minus realized) is the more interpretable descriptive signal.
